name: meeple-loop-v1
description: ⚠️ THIS OVERLAY IS NOW A NO-OP. Dean ruled the meeple loop in on 04/09/2026 and rules.turn.visitCurrency 'meeple' is the shipped default, so setting it here changes nothing at all: running this arm reproduces the base game exactly, and any delta it prints against the reference is sampling noise and nothing else. It is KEPT rather than deleted because six reports in reports/ name it in their filenames and their headers, and a named arm that has vanished is worse than one that does nothing. If you want the game this arm was measured against, it is overlays/v31-card-visit.overlay.json, which is now the control. The rest of this description is the arm as it was written on 04/09/2026 and is kept verbatim as the record of what was tested. THE STRENGTHENED VISIT (Dean's design of 04/09/2026, docs/meeple-loop-visit-handoff-2026-09-04-v1.md). This is the work the v31 plan doc recorded as owed, and it SUPERSEDES the 03/09 standing decision 'leave the free Draw 1 alone and fix the visit side': the free Draw 1 is deleted outright here, on Dean's own call. THE DIAGNOSIS IT IS BUILT ON. The v31 hook fails because the visit is CONDITIONAL and the free Draw 1 is NOT, and because being visited pays the host NOTHING. It was never the card cost. On reference-v11 seeds the shipped game reads Draw 1 on 67.8% of turns against a rival visit's 40.4%, hook 0.41 against a floor of 0.5; handing every seat both bonus options for free (bonus-both-v1) bought only +0.03, which says the visit's problem is availability and payment, not price. WHAT THE ARM CHANGES, ALL AT ONCE, so a null result is informative and a positive one is not attributable. Meeples become the visit currency and no card is ever placed on a Notice Board. Each player starts holding one meeple of each of the five colours and may NEVER hold two of a colour: a duplicate goes to the box, from the board or from the island alike, which is the answer to the pile the old uncapped supply made. The Notice Board stops being a building entirely - no threshold, no stack, no sow, no harvest, no clog - and becomes five colour-keyed slots, one meeple deep. The bonus slot becomes exactly two options: VISIT, placing a meeple on a NEIGHBOUR'S board (never your own) and taking that colour's action, or COLLECT, sweeping your own board back into your supply and drawing 1. Any two meeples spend as one of any colour and both land in the slot bought. The turn-start 'spend any number of meeples, each removed from the game' step is deleted, so a meeple is now never destroyed by being spent: it moves to a neighbour and comes back to them on their collect. The island seeds one meeple per tile on the 3 VP second space rather than two per tile. The Orchard door drops from Draw 3 to Draw 2, because the self-cancellation reason for the exception was that a visit cost a card, and it no longer does. READ IN THIS ORDER, and read the noise floor line before any of them. (1) THE HOOK, rival visits per player per turn: under 0.5 it has not worked, and self-visits should read exactly 0 by construction. (2) THE BONUS MIX four ways - visit a rival / collect with meeples / collect an empty board / slot unspent - where the empty-board collect is the solitaire line that has eaten this slot in every previous version of the game. (3) THE BLOCKED-WANT RATE AND THE HOLD-OUT RATE AT 2 PLAYERS, which is the one number that decides whether Dean's island alternative has to come back; report it, do not build it. (4) Actions per turn and game length TOGETHER: a high rate with a shorter game is the design working, a high rate with an unchanged length is the extra actions going somewhere other than the island. (5) Median supply held in the last third and meeples boxed per game, which is the check on the cap. (6) The wild share of all spends: under about a fifth and the colour keying is doing work, over about half and the slots probably want to be five unkeyed spaces. (7) Deliveries and the barn glut, because about 29 fee cards a game currently reach barns through the old boards and that flow stops dead. (8) Door mix by colour, where orange and cream are still expected weakest, because Sow and Build spend cards and this design does not fix that. ONE THING IN THE ARM IS NOT IN THE DESIGN: W17 The Pie Shop is retexted to fire when a neighbour visits you, which adds a host-side payment the handoff diagnosed as missing but did not itself prescribe. Read any host-side result with that in mind.
